title: A divisor function of Wigert and higher degree forms
summary: Let $k\in\mathbb{N}$. Wigert's divisor function $d^{\left(\frac{1}{k}\right)}(j)$ counts the number of representations of $j$ of the form $m^k+mn$ with $m\geq1 , n\geq0$. Let $\mathcal{F}_k(s)$ denote the Dirichlet series of $d^{\left(\frac{1}{k}\right)}(j)$. While $\mathcal{F}_2(s)$ is essentially a well-known special case of the Euler-Zagier double zeta function, and hence well-studied, very little is known about $\mathcal{F}_k(s)$ for $k>2$.
